summary: This note is a short biographical sketch of Weng Tojirakarn, a Thai activist born to poor Chinese immigrants. It covers his education at Triam Udom Suksa School and Mahidol University's Ramathibodi medical faculty, his leadership of the Medical Students Centre of Thailand, and his self-described discipleship of Buddhadasa Bhikku. It also notes his participation in the 1973 and 1976 Thai student protests.
one_line: Biographical note on Thai student activist and physician Weng Tojirakarn, his education, Buddhist influences, and participation in 1970s protests.
key_facts: Weng Tojirakarn was born into a family of poor Chinese immigrants.
Weng Tojirakarn was admitted to the prestigious Triam Udom Suksa School for his outstanding intelligence.
Weng Tojirakarn studied at the Faculty of Medicine Ramathibodi Hospital, Mahidol University.
Weng Tojirakarn was the secretary-general of the Medical Students Centre of Thailand.
Weng Tojirakarn considered himself a disciple of the Buddhist monk Buddhadasa Bhikku.
Weng Tojirakarn thinks the influence of Buddhadasa's teachings motivated his political and social activism.
Weng Tojirakarn participated in the pro-democracy uprising in October 1973.
Weng Tojirakarn participated in the student protests in 1976.
The 1976 student protests led to the Thammasat University massacre.
The 1976 student protests led to the return to military rule in Thailand.
